paths.title: Sampling and Estimation
paths.description: Connect sampling design, estimator behavior, standard error, and interval estimates.
concept: An estimate describes a population only when the sampling process supports that population claim.
Large convenience samples can be precise about the wrong group.
workflow: Assess both numerical precision and design quality.
A narrow confidence interval does not correct selection bias.
Compute the estimate and standard error.
State the population to which results generalize.
question: Distinguish standard deviation and standard error
What does the standard error of a sample mean describe?
Variation among individual observations
Variation of the sample mean across repeated samples
The largest observed value
The probability the null is true
Standard error measures the sampling variability of an estimator.
checklist: Report enough information to judge an estimate.
Precision, design, and practical context should appear together.
Standard error or interval is reported.

paths.title: Hypothesis Testing and Multiplicity
paths.description: Use tests as calibrated evidence procedures rather than automatic decision machines.
concept: A p-value is conditional on a model
A p-value measures how incompatible the observed data are with a specified null model under its assumptions.
It is not the probability that the null is true or a measure of practical importance.
workflow: Tie the test to a question, effect, and assumptions.
The test statistic is only one part of the conclusion.
Define the estimand and null hypothesis.
Choose the test before viewing outcomes.
Calculate the test statistic and p-value.
question: Handle multiple comparisons
Testing many independent hypotheses without adjustment primarily increases which risk?
False-positive findings
Measurement precision
Sample representativeness
Data storage size
More opportunities to reject increase the false-positive burden unless multiplicity is addressed.
checklist: Verify that the conclusion is stronger than a threshold statement.
Statistical significance should not replace effect interpretation.
The hypothesis was defined before testing.
Effect size and interval accompany the p-value.
Non-significance is not called proof of no effect.

paths.title: Regression and Model Diagnostics
paths.description: Interpret regression parameters while checking residuals, specification, and influence.
concept: A coefficient describes how the modeled outcome changes with a predictor while other included predictors are held fixed.
Its meaning depends on coding, scale, interactions, functional form, and assumptions.
workflow: Inspect whether the model represents the data adequately.
Good fit statistics do not guarantee valid residual behavior or causal interpretation.
Validate on held-out or resampled data.
question: Interpret an interaction
A model includes x, group, and x×group. What does the interaction coefficient represent?
The overall mean outcome
The difference in the x slope between groups
The sample size
The residual standard deviation
The interaction changes the effect or slope of x according to group membership.
checklist: Make coefficient interpretation and uncertainty auditable.
Report model limitations and diagnostics, not only a coefficient table.
Outcome and predictor coding are documented.
Predictions are evaluated out of sample.
